neighbours.label: The verb 'cause' (cause, causes, caused, causing) as a causative verb, vs synonyms (lead to, result in) and the noun 'cause'
fire: Drinking too much coffee can cause headaches in some people.
The broken pipe caused water damage in the basement.
Loud music for hours may cause permanent hearing loss.
A small spark can cause a huge forest fire in summer.
The new policy caused confusion among the staff.
Some cleaning products cause skin irritation.
The storm is causing delays at every airport in the region.
Ice on the bridge caused several accidents this morning.
quiet: Drinking too much coffee can lead to headaches in some people.
The broken pipe resulted in water damage in the basement.
Loud music for hours may lead to permanent hearing loss.
A small spark can start a huge forest fire in summer.
The new policy brought confusion among the staff.
She gave her prize money to a cause she believed in.
The storm is the reason for delays at every airport in the region.
Police are still looking into the cause of the accidents this morning.

predictions: Verb 'cause' 0.35-0.6; 'lead to'/'result in' and the noun 'cause' (good cause, the cause of) under 0.16.
notes: Card: ' cause' x19, ' causing' x5, ' caused' x4, ' causes' x3. Probe: 'rain caused flooding' 0.568, 'may cause high blood pressure' 0.501, 'can cause lung cancer' 0.395; 'may lead to' 0.061, 'resulted in' 0.113, noun 'The cause of the fire' 0.154, 'a good cause' 0.001, 'because' -0.001. So it is the verb word, not the causal meaning.
